title: Find the earliest unique event
prompt: Given an array of event labels, return the index of the first label that appears exactly once in the entire array. Return -1 if there is none. Labels are case-sensitive strings. For ['open', 'save', 'open', 'close', 'save'], return 3. The array may be empty. Explain your approach, implement it, and test the all-repeated case.
followUps: Why does the result depend on the original order?
What happens when all labels are different?
How much memory is required when every label is distinct?

twist.prompt: Events now arrive as a stream. After every event, report the earliest label that is still unique without rescanning the entire stream.

hints: Separate counting from preserving the original order.
A map can tell you whether a label occurs more than once.
For the streaming version, consider a queue whose front can be discarded when it is no longer unique.
